page: Microsoft Azure E96-24as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the EASv4 series, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance isolates 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. While the standard E96 footprint exposes 96 vCPUs, this constrained vCPU variant retains the full memory complement of 672.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields a massive 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, designed specifically for workloads requiring high memory capacity without the licensing overhead of large core counts.

The compute subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with instruction set support including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. CPU benchmarking demonstrates strong single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 2925.68, while the 24-thread multi-core score registers at 32485.3. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high efficiency, recording a PassMark memory score of 2927.53 and an uncached large-block read throughput of 78.04 GB/sec alongside 44.95 GB/sec of write bandwidth.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 1443 GB solid-state drive (SSD), providing fast scratch space for intermediate operations. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units (GPU count is 0) or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic execution tests demonstrate robust in-memory metrics, achieving 24.0 million operations per second on Redis SET evaluations and 10508.95 on PassMark database routines. For language model execution, text generation on small models hits 298.02 tokens per second, but throughput drops to 4.97 tokens per second for prompt processing on 70B parameter models due to core count and vector limitations.

The constrained-core architecture offers distinct cost efficiencies when running software products licensed on a per-core basis, such as commercial relational databases. Workloads ideally suited for the E96-24as_v4 include large-scale in-memory databases like Redis or SAP HANA, high-capacity caching tiers, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise database systems requiring low CPU-to-memory ratios.
